archetype.name: Play-In Team (one-way)
archetype.definition: A team whose league-average offense and ball security keep it near the play-in line, while a bottom-five defense and the league's worst defensive rebounding keep it from being anything more.

report.headline: An average offense undone by the league's worst defensive glass
report.take:
Phoenix at 5-7 is about what its play says it is, maybe a hair better. The margin implies four wins and the W vs Pt Diff of 1 credits one extra, mostly from a 102-99 win over Houston and a 101-96 win over Charlotte. A Net Rtg of -4.8 (22nd) and a site rank of 23rd describe a team on the wrong side of the play-in line. The offense is exactly league average: an ORtg of 114.2 against a league mark of 114.2. The defense is the problem, with a DRtg of 119.0 (26th).

The defense breaks down in two places. The first is the glass. Phoenix grabs 66.9% of opponents' misses, last in the league and 5.9 points below average, and its REB % of 45.8 is also last. Last season's team rebounded 71.9% of misses on defense and finished 10th in Def Rank, so this is a real step back, not a holdover. The second is the point of attack. Opposing point guards average 32.92 points a game against Phoenix, the most in the league, and take 28.1% of the points against it compared with 22.7% league-wide. Centers do 25.08 points and 16.25 rebounds a game, both 29th. What the defense does well gets buried under that. Opp Rim FG % is a respectable 63.6 (13th), and it forces turnovers at the sixth-best rate. Those extra possessions are mostly handed back on the defensive boards.

The group grades say the same thing: backcourt C+, wings C-, frontcourt D+. Devin Booker (10th of 109 at his position, 60.9 TS % on 29.0 USG %) and Miles Bridges (9th of 88) are carrying their groups. Around them the heavy minutes go to players with poor numbers. Jalen Green has played 320 minutes at a 48.8 TS % and -5.7 BPM. Dillon Brooks has played 350 at a -4.5 BPM. Their On-Off marks of -34.0 and -23.9 line up with the box score, so that read is more than noise. Booker's -25.2 On-Off almost certainly reflects who shares the floor with him. Meanwhile Ryan Dunn (+28.2), Luke Kennard (67.9 TS %) and Collin Gillespie (+13.5) have been the better lineups in fewer minutes.

The direction is better than the record. October was a 1-3 month allowing 124.5 a game. November is 4-4, scoring 113.0 and allowing 113.75, essentially level with the league. The last five games allowed 111.6 a game, 5.73 fewer than the season rate. Most of that came on a long homestand, though. The only road games in the last ten were losses at Oklahoma City and Golden State. This week sends Phoenix out on four road games to find out whether the November defense travels.

strengths.title: Booker and Bridges are top-ten caliber
strengths.body: Booker is 10th of 109 shooting guards, scoring efficiently (60.9 TS %) on a heavy 29.0 USG %. Bridges is 9th of 88 power forwards, with a 2.4 BPM and a team-high share of frontcourt rebounds. Their production is steady and should hold. The issue is how little help surrounds them, not their own level.

strengths.title: Wins the turnover battle
strengths.body: Phoenix gives the ball away rarely, with a TOV % of 12.6 (9th). It also forces turnovers at the sixth-best rate, an Opp TOV % of 14.8. That is a structural edge that should last, and it keeps an otherwise average offense from slipping below average. It is also the main reason the rebounding deficit hasn't sunk the team entirely.

strengths.title: Defense trending toward respectable
strengths.body: After allowing 124.5 a game in October, Phoenix allowed 113.75 a game in November and 111.6 over the last five. Rim protection is already middle of the pack (Opp Rim FG % 63.6, 13th), so the base is sounder than the 26th-ranked DRtg suggests. Some of the drop came against home opponents, so treat it as a promising sign rather than settled.

concerns.title: Worst defensive rebounding in the league
concerns.body: A DRB % of 66.9 ranks 30th and sits 5.9 points below average. It feeds a league-worst REB % and RPG. Opposing centers average 16.25 rebounds a game, 29th. The roster lacks size and the frontcourt grades D+. This doesn't fix itself without lineup changes, though last season's 71.9 shows the organization can be closer to average.

concerns.title: Point guards are feasting
concerns.body: Opposing PGs score 32.92 a game, the most allowed in the league, and take 28.1% of the points against Phoenix. Combined with an Opp 3P % of 37.6 (26th), perimeter containment is the leak. Part of that is opponent shooting variance that should cool. The share of points is too lopsided to be all luck.

concerns.title: Heavy minutes for the weakest links
concerns.body: Jalen Green ranks 99th of 109 at his position. He has a 48.8 TS %, a -5.7 BPM and a -34.0 On-Off, yet has the second-most backcourt minutes. Brooks's -4.5 BPM drags the wings to a C-. Kennard and Dunn post far better numbers in fewer minutes. Until that rotation shifts, the supporting cast stays a net negative.

trend.note: A 1-3 October with a leaky defense gave way to a .500 November in which Phoenix allowed points at roughly league average. The last five sit at 3-2 with a near-even margin, but most of that came at home.

weekAhead.headline: Four road games, three against the West's basement
weekAhead.body:
The trip opens at Denver (7-4, 15th on the site), the only opponent with a winning record. After that come Sacramento (1-12, 30th), Utah (1-13, 27th) and New Orleans (4-10, 25th). Sacramento and Utah have the 27th and 29th ranked offenses. That is exactly the kind of opposition a 26th-ranked defense needs to prove its November improvement was real.

The catch is the road. The only away games in Phoenix's last ten were losses, and the recent defensive gains came almost entirely at home. A 3-1 week is there for the taking. Anything less than two wins against this group would say the November numbers were mostly the schedule and the building.

keyMatchups.title: Denver shuts down guards, not forwards
keyMatchups.body: Denver holds point guards 6.12 points under their averages, best in the league, and lets shooting guards score just 19.64 a game (3rd). That is a tough night for Booker. The opening is up front: Denver allows 27.82 points a game to power forwards (29th) and the most threes to the position. This sets up a Bridges game.

keyMatchups.title: Get to the rim against Sacramento
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento keeps opponents out of the paint better than anyone, with an Opp Rim Rate of 22.5 (1st). When teams do get there, they shoot 74.8%, the worst Opp Rim FG % in the league. Its 57.4 Opp eFG % is also last. A Phoenix offense that rarely draws fouls (FT Rate 28th) should still find easy points here.

keyMatchups.title: New Orleans' frontcourt and free throws
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans has a B+ frontcourt and leads the league in FT Rate at 37.2. That pressures a Phoenix team with the worst DRB % and a D+ frontcourt. On the other end, the Pelicans' 30th-ranked defense gives power forwards 29.5 points a game, also last. That makes the finale a shootout Bridges can tilt.

weekAhead.watch: Phoenix's defensive rebounding on the road. If it can't hold the glass against Sacramento and Utah, the November defensive gains were mostly the homestand.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is genuinely average and should stay there. Booker and Bridges are producing at a high level, the turnover edge is structural, and the shooting numbers (eFG % 54.3, 3P % 36.0) are in line with recent seasons. The free-throw shortage is a long-standing trait, not a slump. The defense decides the season. Its November form, allowing points at about league average, is closer to last year's 10th-ranked unit than October was. Some of the Opp 3P % damage should regress in Phoenix's favor. The defensive rebounding is a roster problem, though, and won't simply revert.

The current pace points to 34 wins. I expect a bit better, somewhere in the mid-to-high 30s, as the defense settles toward the middle of the league and the schedule softens. With the W vs Pt Diff already slightly positive, there is no hidden bad luck to bank on. It is a play-in chase, and getting there probably requires shifting minutes from Green and Brooks toward the lineups that have actually won their minutes.
swingFactors: Defensive rebounding getting anywhere near league average
Rotation minutes shifting from Green and Brooks to Dunn and Kennard
Whether the November defense holds up on the road

confidence.note: Twelve games; the shape is consistent, but On-Off figures and opponent shooting are noisy this early.
